# Medical Standard Operating Procedure
This procedure applies to the Chief Medical Officer, Medical Doctors, Chemists, Paramedics, Interns, and any crew member acting in a medical capacity.
## Duty of Care
Medical personnel [bold]shall[/bold] treat any patient brought to them, regardless of who that patient is or what they are accused of having done. Triage is decided by severity, not by rank, department, or personal preference.
[italic]A restrained prisoner bleeding out is treated before a Head of Staff with a bruise. Security may supervise; they may not order the patient turned away.[/italic]
Refusing treatment to a living patient is a serious breach and is grounds for demotion by the Chief Medical Officer or the Captain.
## Prisoners and Non-Crew
Prisoners [bold]must[/bold] be given medical treatment before serving a sentence, as required by [textlink="Security Standard Operating Procedure" link="GuideSecuritySOP"]. Medical [italic]should[/italic] request a Security escort rather than refuse the patient.
Non-crew lifeforms are treated where they present themselves peacefully for treatment. Medical is [italic]not[/italic] obliged to pursue them, and [italic]should not[/italic] detain them for study.
## Chemistry and Controlled Substances
Chemists [italic]should[/italic] keep the medical supply stocked before filling personal or novelty requests.
Chemistry [bold]shall not[/bold] produce or distribute substances whose primary use is harm — this includes but is not limited to poisons, corrosives, and incendiary mixtures — except on the order of the Chief Medical Officer or Commanding Officer, and only for a stated purpose.
[italic]Producing napalm because Security asked nicely is not a stated purpose. Producing a measured quantity of a caustic agent for a documented Engineering task is.[/italic]
Recreational and non-medical chemistry is permitted at the Chief Medical Officer's discretion, provided it does not consume stock the department needs. See [textlink="Permits" link="GuidePermits"] for anything on the controlled list.
## Cybernetics, Implants and Body Modification
Elective augmentation requires the patient's clear consent. Fitting an implant into an unconscious or restrained patient without cause is [bold]not[/bold] permitted.
Implant [italic]searches[/italic] are a Security procedure and require a warrant, or the suspect's consent, before Medical will participate. The rules are in [textlink="Security Standard Operating Procedure" link="GuideSecuritySOP"] — Medical personnel [bold]shall[/bold] see the warrant before operating.
Mindshield implants are fitted at the direction of Command or Security. Medical does not issue them on its own initiative.
Requests for advanced cybernetics or experimental hardware go through Epistemics. See [textlink="Science SOP" link="GuideEpistemicsSOP"].
## Cloning and Handling of the Dead
Bodies [bold]shall not[/bold] be cloned, revived, or disposed of over the objection of the deceased's own wishes where those are known.
Medical [italic]shall not[/italic] destroy, gib, or space a body that could still be revived, and [italic]should[/italic] hold remains in Medical or the morgue rather than leaving them in corridors.
Security may place a hold on a body that is evidence in an ongoing case. Medical [italic]should[/italic] honour that hold where the patient cannot be revived, and [italic]should[/italic] override it where they can.
## Records and Confidentiality
Medical records are departmental property. They [italic]should not[/italic] be read out over general comms or handed to crew with no need to know.
Command and Security [italic]may[/italic] request records relevant to an active incident. Blanket requests for the whole crew's medical history [italic]should[/italic] be refused unless the Captain orders otherwise in writing.
## Cryogenics
Cryogenic pods are for stabilising patients Medical cannot otherwise treat. They are [italic]not[/italic] storage for inconvenient crew.
Placing a conscious, unwilling crew member into cryogenics is treated as an unlawful detention and will be handled under [textlink="Space Law" link="SpaceLaw"].
## Departmental Conduct
Medical Interns [bold]shall not[/bold] perform procedures they have not been cleared for by the Chief Medical Officer or a Medical Doctor.
Medical personnel [italic]should not[/italic] leave the department unstaffed. Where a Paramedic is unavailable, one Doctor [italic]may[/italic] respond off-department, provided someone remains to receive patients.
